Vide this JudgmentcumAward, I shall decide the Detailed Accidental Report (in short, the DAR)/petition under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, (in short, the Act) filed by petitioner/Sanjeev for grant of compensation for the injuries suffered by him in the road vehicular accident which occurred on 09.04.2010.

2. It is stated that it is stated that the petitioner was going to Haiderpur on his vehicle bearing no.
DL1LK4487 i.e. Tata Ace (in short, the said vehicle) on 09.04.2010 at 03:30 pm and when he was Sh. Sanjeev vs Sh. Jagpal on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192651295/
1 crossing the Britannia Flyover, then a canter bearing no. UP14BT 0056 (in short the offending vehicle) driven by respondent no.1 at a high speed, in zigzag manner, rashly and negligently,
without proper look out, without taking care of the persons traveling on road, had over taken the said vehicle of the petitioner, and started driving ahead of the said vehicle, but the respondent no.1 had suddenly applied brakes upon the offending vehicle.

As a result of such sudden application of brakes by respondent no.1, the said vehicle collided with the offending vehicle and furthermore, as a result of such MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 2 of 14 collision, some unknown vehicle plied by some unknown person, hit the said vehicle from behind.
As a result of such collision, the petitioner sustained injuries in his right leg.

The petitioner was immediately taken to the Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, where his MLC No. 324/2010 was prepared by the doctors and the petitioner remained admitted there from 10.04.2010 to 28.04.2010 and during this period, a surgery was performed in the right leg of the petitioner.
3. It is stated that case FIR No.451/2010 u/s 279/338 IPC was registered against the unknown vehicle, which was running behind the said vehicle, however, as per the statement of the petitioner,
the above said accident was solely caused due to the negligence of the respondent no.1, but the police took signatures of the petitioner on some blank papers, and the IO made the petitioner not only the accused but also the witness in the above case.

The police officials did not carry out the investigation in proper manner, and the Hon'ble Court vide order dated 13.03.2012 had also found that IO of the case had not carry out the investigation in proper manner, and he deliberately favoured the driver and owner of the offending vehicle and further directed IO to carry out investigation in proper manner.
4. It is stated that the petitioner at the time of said accident was 32 years old and was working as a driver and earning an amount of Rs. 6,000/ per month.

The petitioner could not resume his work ever since the accident took place and due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.

6. It is stated that the respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 being the driver and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

The respondent no.1 was driving the said offending vehicle during the accident in the course of employment, supervision, management and control of respondent no.2, the respondent no.3 being the insurer/Insurance Co. is also vicariously liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner may be compensated for physical injury, pecuniary, nonpecuniary damages, mental agony and trauma.

7. The respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 have appeared but they did not file any written statement.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.3/Insurance Company and, inter alia, it is submitted that the present petition is not maintainable as there is no cause of action ever arose in the favour of the petitioner and against the respondent no.3 to file the present petition.
It is submitted that the IO has filed chargesheet against the petitioner/driver of the said vehicle before the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate.

As per chargesheet, the driver of the said vehicle was not hit by some other vehicle from behind, and the petitioner received injury due to his own negligence by hitting the MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 4 of 14 offending vehicle from behind.
So, the present case is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed with cost.
9. It is submitted that the petition is time barred and not covered under the limitation.

In the present petition, as per record, date of accident is 09.04.2010, however, the FIR was registered on 28.11.2010 and the petitioner has filed present petition in August 2018 after 7 years of the accident only to extract unjustified compensation from the respondent no.3.
The present petition is bad for the nonjoinder of the necessary parties.

Hence, the claim is liable to be dismissed against respondent no.3.
10.

It is submitted that the petitioner at the time of accident was responsible for the accident and,
therefore, compromised with the owner of the offending vehicle, but, thereafter, he has filed petition to extract money from the respondent no.3.
The cause of accident was sole negligence of the petitioner/ Driver of the said vehicle, who has been held negligent even by the Investigation Officer as per the chargesheet.
Hence, the driver of the said vehicle/petitioner was fully responsible and negligent for the said accident, therefore, respondent no.3 is not liable for compensation.

11. It is submitted that all the available documents, FIR, Statement of Eye Witness, Head Constables and the chargesheet clearly made the petitioner, responsible for the said accident that had occurred on 09.04.2010.

The respondent no.1 and 2 are proceeded ex MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no.

then the respondent no.3 has every right to take all the defences available to the respondent no. 1 and 2 as per u/s 170 of the Act.
The respondent no.3 has every right to take defence available to as per u/s 149(2) of the Act.

12. It is submitted that, in case, the award is passed alongwith interest in favour of the petitioner then the interest must according to rate of interest applicable at present of the R.B.I. or Nationalised Bank and not more than prescribed rate.

The petitioner has filed the present petition against the respondents and onus is upon the petitioner to prove rash and negligent act of respondent no.1.
PW1 has reaffirmed and reiterated the averments made in the DAR as well as in the petition.
21. The respondents have filed their respective written statements denying the allegations levelled by the petitioner in the DAR/petition.

22. Furthermore, it is an established principle of law that in a claim petition under the Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt.
In case of Kaushnamma Begum and others V/s
New India
Assurance Company Limited" (2001) 2 SCC 9

, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Act.
MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 8 of 14 23.

v. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Anr., 2019 SCC Online SC 195, wherein, it has been observed as under :
"20.....

v. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Anr., 2019 SCC Online SC 195
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While dealing with a claim petition in terms of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a tribunal stricto sensu is not bound by the pleadings of the parties; its function being to determine the amount of fair compensation in the event an accident has taken place by reason of negligence of that driver of a motor vehicle.

It is true that occurrence of an accident having regard to the provisions contained in Section 166 of the Act is a sine qua non for entertaining a claim petition but that would not mean that despite evidence to the effect that death of the claimant's predecessor had taken place by reason of an accident caused by a motor vehicle, the same would be ignored only on the basis of a postmortem report visavis the averments made in a claim Sh. Sanjeev vs Sh. Jagpal on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192651295/
5 petition.
XXXXX 14

. Some discrepancies in the evidence of the claimant's witnesses might have occurred but the core question before the Tribunal and consequently before the High Court was as to whether the bus in question was involved in the accident or not.

For the purpose of determining the said issue, the Court was required to apply the principle underlying the burden of proof in terms of the provisions of Section 106 of the Evidence Act, 1872 as to whether a dead body wrapped in a blanket had been found at the spot at such an early hour, which was required to be proved by Respondents 2 and 3.
15.
In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
For the said purpose, the High Court should have taken into consideration the respective stories set forth by both the parties."
(emphasis supplied)

The Court restated the legal position that the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt cannot be applied by the Tribunal while dealing with the motor accident cases.
Even in that case, the view taken by MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 9 of 14 the High Court to reverse similar findings, recorded by the Tribunal was set aside."
24. Now, I would like to advert to the facts and circumstances of the present DAR.

25. Petitioner/PW1 testified that the said car was driven by petitioner on 09.04.2010 and at about 3:30 pm, when he was crossing the Britannia Flyover, then, in the meantime, the driver of the offending vehicle overtook the said car from behind and, thereafter, applied brake on the offending vehicle and, resultantly, the said car collided with the offending vehicle from behind and, thereafter,
one unknown vehicle which was following the said car also hit the said car from behind and the petitioner suffered grievous injuries.

26. However, as per the final report filed by IO, which is part and parcel of the DAR, on receipt of DD No.26A PS Saraswati Vihar, which contained details that on 09.04.2010 at about 4:35 PM, one accident happened near Britannia Chowk and the injured is being taken to the Hospital.

Thereafter,
HC Jagdish approached the spot of accident, where it was informed that injured has been shifted to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital.

IO went to hospital and it transpired that the injured/petitioner/driver of the offending vehicle submitted that the matter has been settled between them and the accident Sh. Sanjeev vs Sh. Jagpal on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192651295/
6 call was filed through DD No.49B.
MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 10 of 14 27.

It may be noted that, thereafter, petitioner appeared in PS Saraswati Vihar on 29.11.2010 and made a statement that he was driving the said car on 09.04.2010, and the driver of the offending vehicle suddenly applied brake and the said car collided with the offending vehicle at about 3:30 pm near Ring Road, CNG Petrol Pump, and one unknown vehicle, which was moving behind the said car hit the said car, and the said car got entangled with the offending vehicle.
28.

It may be also relevant to mention here that the petitioner has improved his first version recorded by police over his version given in his testimony in as much as in his first statement before police, he stated that he compromised with respondent no.1, whereas, in his deposition, he testified that the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent after overtaking the said car of petitioner,
suddenly applied the brakes, and the said car driven by petitioner collided with the offending vehicle, however, in the meantime, some unknown vehicle hit the said car from behind.

Even if, for the sake of arguments, it is presumed that the version given by the petitioner to the IO on the basis,
the DD no. 26A filed by DD no. 49B is not at variance with his deposition, even then, the petitioner has failed to prove that it was negligence of the respondent no.1 or the driver of the unknown vehicle on account of which petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 11 of 14 29.

It may be noted that petitioner has led no evidence except his solitary statement that the said car collided with the offending vehicle as respondent, who was driving the offending vehicle, suddenly applied the brakes, and, resultantly, the unknown vehicle following the said car hit the said car from behind and the said car collided with and entangled in the offending vehicle.
30.

It may be also relevant to mention here that apart from the oral evidence, documentary evidence, which is a part and parcel of the DAR, namely the mechanical inspection of the said car and offending vehicle, also did not support the petitioner that he suffered injuries on account of the rash and negligence driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

The said car was mechanically inspected on 02.12.2010 albeit after about more than seven month of the said accident, however, no fresh damage/dent has been found either in front of the said car or on the back side of the said car.
In addition to it, the offending vehicle was inspected on 27.12.2012 whose right side rear safety rod was found dented and rod bracket was also found bended.

Therefore, a bare perusal of the mechanical inspection reports of the said car and offending vehicle lead to conclude that it was the said car driven by petitioner, which hit the offending vehicle, and the back side of the offending vehicle was found having dent marks.
Sh. Sanjeev vs Sh. Jagpal on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192651295/
7 31.

Apart from that, it may also be noted that the petitioner has MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no.
451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..

Page no. 12 of 14 faced the trail in the above said FIR, and he pleaded guilty before ld. Metropolitan Magistrate in terms of his statement dated 08.02.2017 i.e. Ex. RW1/1 recorded by ld. Metropolitan Magistrate.
The petitioner in his statement before the ld. Metropolitan Magistrate has pleaded guilty that he was driving the said car in a rash and negligent manner, and he was punished under Section 279 IPC.

It may be noted that the petitioner not only plead guilty in the above said criminal trial before the ld. Metropolitan Magistrate but also never filed any protest petition in the said criminal trial that the investigation carried out by the IO is shoddy one or IO has conducted no investigation as per the facts disclosed by the petitioner.
32.

In view of the above, it may be concluded that it was rash and negligent driving of the petitioner,
on account of which the said car hit the offending vehicle from behind, and got entangled in the offending vehicle, therefore, the petitioner failed to prove on record that he suffered grievous injuries on account of the rash and negligent driving by the respondent no.1.
Issue no.1 is accordingly decided in favour of the respondents and against the petitioner.
ISSUE NO.2 33.
In view of the findings on issue, not, the respondents are not held liable to indemnify the petitioners, therefore, issue no. 2 is also decided in favour of the petitioner and against petitioner.
MACT Case No.600/2018 (FIR no. 451/2010) Sanjeev v. Jagpal & Ors..
Page no. 13 of 14 RELIEF 34.
In view of the findings on issue no.1 & issue no.2, the present DAR/petition filed by the petitioner is accordingly dismissed.
